gaps.sentence: It was the first time she ___ a car on her own.
gaps.hint: it was the first time takes past perfect
gaps.explanation: After 'It was the first time' in past contexts, English uses the past perfect: had driven.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to Greece for our honeymoon, but that was twenty years ago.
gaps.hint: twenty years ago fixes a finished past
gaps.explanation: A finished time expression like 'twenty years ago' demands the past simple: went.

gaps.sentence: Hardly ___ the presentation started when the fire alarm went off.
gaps.explanation: 'Hardly had … when' — the past perfect with inversion after 'hardly'.

gaps.sentence: I can't talk now — I ___ dinner for twelve people.
gaps.hint: now plus a temporary activity in progress
gaps.explanation: 'Now' marks a temporary action in progress, so the present continuous is needed: am cooking.

gaps.sentence: I ___ dinner when the lights went out.
gaps.hint: the lights went out interrupted it
gaps.explanation: The lights going out interrupted an ongoing background action, so the past continuous is used: was cooking.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, with my phone switched off.
gaps.hint: this time next week means in progress
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous fits: will be lying.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ a lot since the new road opened.
gaps.hint: since clause with a present result
gaps.explanation: Change that started in the past and continues to now takes the present perfect: has changed.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her grandmother every Sunday; it is a promise she never breaks.
gaps.hint: every Sunday marks repeated routine action
gaps.explanation: 'Every Sunday' signals a regularly repeated action, so the present simple is correct: visits.
